plan: My value is $44. This is a second-price auction with common value elements. In a standard private-value second-price auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy. However, because values are positively correlated (common value component), there is a risk of the "winner's curse." But in a second-price auction, the winner's curse is mitigated because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Given the value range (0-29 common + 0-20 taste = max 49), $44 is very high. I will bid my true value to maximize the probability of winning profitably.

My value is $47. Since this is a single-round game, I need to balance winning with not overpaying. Given the possible value range (0-69), a bid close to my value is reasonable. I'll bid slightly above what I estimate the others might bid, aiming to win against potentially conservative bidders. I’ll bid $42. This leaves room for others to bid higher, but still gives me a good chance to win without excessive payment.

My value is $40. Since this is the only round, I need to bid aggressively but not overpay. I anticipate other bidders' values will be somewhat correlated with mine. A bid slightly above the expected second-highest bid is optimal. Given the possible range of values (0-60), and assuming a somewhat uniform distribution, I'll bid a bit above what I think the others might reasonably offer. I'll bid $35.
